description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to strengthen Ethiopia's institutional capacity for disaster risk management, and flood risk management in selected basins.

The project was originally approved as an Investment Project Financing (IPF) for an International Development Association (IDA) grant of US$300 million. At the request of the GoE, US$100 million are being cancelled from the project. The project development objective and development outcomes remain the same. The project will end as per the original scheduled end date of March 31, 2028.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2 Section I.B.2 (a) of the Financing Agreement: The Recipient shall, not later than sixty (60) days after the EffectiveDate, (and thereafter by April 30th of each subsequent EFY) prepare and furnish to the Association, an annual work plan and budgetcontaining all activities (including Subprojects) proposed for implementation in the following calendar year including: (i) adetailed timetable for the sequencing and implementation of said activities; (ii) the types of expenditures required for suchactivities, including a proposed financing plan; and (iii) a budget establishing the proposed amounts and sources of financing.

Schedule 2 Section I.E.5 of the Financing Agreement: The Recipient shall, by no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date,establish, publicize, maintain, and operate an accessible grievance mechanism, to receive and facilitate resolution of concerns andgrievances of Project-affected people, and take all measures necessary and appropriate to resolve, or facilitate the resolution of,such concerns and grievances, in a manner acceptable to the Association.

1.1 Strengthened institutional and coordination capacity for disaster risk management

baseline.value: - DRM is neither mainstreamed into sectors, nor monitored and evaluated across levels of government - Sharing of disaster risk information is not fully carried out and data is not utilized among government entities - DRF instruments are weak - EP&R capacity is characterized by a lack of basic emergency response resources

target.value: - DRM is mainstreamed into selected sectoral instruments and tools to inform development planning process and future investment decisions. -Progress made in DRM is monitored and evaluated across various levels of government - Disaster risk information is shared among selected government entities and utilized for development planning and decision making - One DRF instrument is strengthened - EP&R capacity for search and rescue is strengthened
